thread:
Alex M: Heads-up — noticed p50/p95 look fine but p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~300ms after the streaming rollout. Dashboard backend p99 stable, endpoint p99 up.
Priya S: Saw that too. My hypothesis: frontend includes stream closing/flush time. Backend measures until last token emitted; client measures until stream close + ack.
Sam K: Where does the latency metric in the console come from today? We tag `transport` but streaming uses chunked responses, might lack a final `end` event.
Alex M: Logs from a slow trace:
```
server: last_token_emitted=161234567890
client: stream_end_received=161234567930
client: flush_complete=161234567960
```
So about ~70ms between token emission and flush complete in these traces, sometimes higher.
Kate L: We should split `server_processing` vs `delivery` in the dashboard. Also the percentile merge mode matters — t-digest vs raw-sample merges can show different p99s when sample rates differ.
Priya S: Quick A/B in staging: disable client-side flush for streaming -> endpoint p99 returned to baseline. So delivery is majority of delta.
Sam K: Proposal: add tag `delivery_method=streaming|buffered`, emit `server_processing_ms` and `delivery_ms` as separate fields. Update alerts to fire on `server_processing.p99`.
Alex M: +1. Also note router rollout: streaming variant is 10% traffic; merge weights are currently naive and reduce effective sample counts in some rollups — that skews percentiles.
Kate L: Mixing sampled and unsampled groups will bias tdigest merges. We need normalized sample weights or separate rollups by sampling-rate bucket. Filed a ticket (link in thread).
deploy-bot: Deployed telemetry patch to staging at 1745678922 :white_check_mark:
Priya S: Plan:
1) Emit `delivery_method` tag
2) Emit `server_processing_ms` and `delivery_ms`
3) Add dashboard widgets for both and update alert baselines
Who picks up items?
Sam K: I'll do the tag + storage schema change (will need a small migration). Alex M: I'll update dashboard widgets and docs. Priya S: I'll tune alerts and update rollout playbook. Kate L: I'll add a console note explaining pctl derivation and why streaming affects endpoint p99.
Alex M: I'll post screenshots once widgets are ready. TL;DR: p99 spike is delivery-side, not server. Short-term: alert on server_processing.p99, mid-term: breakouts + sampling-normalized merges.
Priya S: Also adding a one-liner to the rollout checklist: "Expect endpoint p99 noise when enabling streaming; use server_processing.p99 for platform health checks."
